title: Runtime: tag perf-canary traffic + propagate runtime_build and scheduler_mode into metrics/tracing
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Motivation: The perf-regression canary needs a clean way to (a) identify canary traffic end-to-end and (b) slice latency/throughput regressions by runtime build + scheduler mode without exploding cardinality for customer traffic. This PR introduces request-scoped tags for canary requests (source=perf-canary) and propagates runtime_build and scheduler_mode through the runtime context into both metrics and tracing. Summary of changes: 1) Request tag propagation: Add RequestTags to the request context (source, canary_run_id, canary_suite). The canary runner will set source=perf-canary; the gateway/service boundary preserves the tag through internal RPC calls. 2) Runtime build identification: Add runtime_build tag (e.g., "runtime@1.18.0+git:6f2c8c1") emitted as a metric label and trace attribute only when source=perf-canary (and for internal traffic). For non-canary/customer traffic, we keep the existing lower-cardinality runtime_version label and do NOT attach runtime_build. 3) Scheduler mode tagging: Add scheduler_mode (e.g., "default", "pinned", "exp-heuristic-x") to canary requests. The scheduler sets this from its effective config (post overrides), and we propagate it via context so it lands consistently in server spans and request-level metrics. 4) Metrics + tracing integration: Metrics: extend inference request metric emission to include source, runtime_build, scheduler_mode when allowed. Tracing: add otel span attributes: redwood.request.source, redwood.runtime.build, redwood.scheduler.mode. We also attach these to the top-level server span to simplify filtering in Tempo. 5) Guardrails / cardinality: Labels are gated behind an allowlist based on source. Explicitly only: source=perf-canary enables runtime_build and scheduler_mode labels. This keeps customer-facing timeseries stable. Notes: This is the foundation PR; follow-ups will add batch stats + kernel selection dumps behind the same source gating. Testing: Added unit tests covering tag propagation across internal RPC boundaries, and a regression test ensuring runtime_build is not emitted for customer traffic. Manual validation: verified in staging that perf-canary requests show up in Grafana when filtered by source=perf-canary and that traces include the attributes on root spans. Rollout: Safe to ship; behavior is opt-in via request tags from the canary runner. No config changes required for existing customer workloads.
commits: runtime: plumb RequestTags through inference request context
telemetry: gate high-cardinality labels behind request source allowlist
scheduler: export effective scheduler mode to request context
tracing: attach canary/source + runtime_build + scheduler_mode to server spans
tests: ensure runtime_build label never emitted for customer traffic
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry): Can we confirm we are not adding runtime_build to customer traffic metrics? That will blow up timeseries. Also please use the standardized attribute keys from the telemetry standards doc.

Omar El-Sayed (Author): Yep—runtime_build + scheduler_mode are gated behind source=perf-canary (and internal). For all other traffic, unchanged labels. I updated attribute keys to redwood.runtime.build and redwood.scheduler.mode and kept source as redwood.request.source.

Nadia Rahman (Metrics): For metrics, please ensure the new labels are only attached to request-level metrics, not all token-level counters. Also, do we have a default scheduler_mode value to avoid empty label churn?
Omar El-Sayed (Author): Good call. Scoped to request latency + throughput metrics only. For scheduler_mode, default is "default" (explicit), so we won’t emit empty/unknown.

Sofia Ivanova (Scheduling): scheduler_mode should reflect effective config (including overrides) rather than the requested mode so we don’t get misleading slices. Can we plumb the effective value after config resolution?
Omar El-Sayed (Author): Updated to set scheduler_mode after scheduler config resolution and added a unit test for the override path.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add a short note on how this interacts with maintenance windows/deploy annotations later, and make sure this doesn’t change alerting baselines for existing SLO metrics.
Omar El-Sayed (Author): Added notes in the PR description and docs. Existing SLO metrics are unchanged; the new labels are only present for perf-canary traffic and are new series.
Caleb Johnson (Tracing): Span attribute cardinality is still a cost concern. Are we sure we want runtime_build on every span?
Omar El-Sayed (Author): Only on the root server span (and only for source=perf-canary). Downstream spans inherit context but we do not attach the attributes broadly. That keeps trace size stable.
